newsitem.title: New Zealand: CRICKET-England's Silverwood hopeful of test call.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-England's Silverwood hopeful of test call.

text.p: PALMERSTON NORTH, Jan 15 - A pair of promising young Yorkshire fast-medium bowlers could yet play a significant part in England's New Zealand cricket tour ambitions, NZPA reports.
While Darren Gough's abilities have already been displayed frequently at test level, 21-year-old Chris Silverwood could finish up as one of the big finds of the tour.
A surprise selection for the tour of Zimbabwe and New Zealand, Silverwood has already achieved his main ambition, to play a test.
He made an encouraging debut in the first test against Zimbabwe at Bulawayo, taking three for 63 in the first innings, four wickets in the match.
He missed the second test but played all three one-day internationals there.
In two innings in New Zealand he has shown lively pace and bounce and is relishing his chance.
He picked up two for 32 in 8.4 overs against the New Zealand Academy at New Plymouth last Friday and two for 24 from 12 overs in the New Zealand Selection 11's first innings 138 here on Monday.
It's still early days in New Zealand but Silverwood has hinted that he could well figure in England's test plans here.
"I knew I'd have to work hard, have to fight my way into the side, which I did in Zimbabwe," Silverwood told NZPA.
"I was chuffed to bits that I got a chance. I've done more up to now than I expected to do all tour to be honest. Everything's a big bonus for me."
Silverwood, an avid Castleford rugby league club supporter, comes from the village of Kippax near Leeds.
After making his senior county debut in 1994 at 18 he quickly signalled his talents with 27 wickets in seven matches.
A back injury curtailed his 1995 season but last year he took 47 wickets in a near-complete championship programme and won two notable awards.
He was named the Cricket Writers Young Player of the Year and the Players' Player of the Year.
"The cricket writers' award is a big honour but the one from the players was special to me because the people I was playing with award that," he said.
Initially he thought he might squeeze a place in the England A squad which toured Australia before Christmas.
Instead the England selectors saw something special and Silverwood made the bigger jump into the senior side.
"This tour is a big learning curve," Silverwood said.

"I'm out here with the cream of the England cricketers, I'm playing a couple of world class sides, I can watch their bowlers and our bowlers, bowl against some of the top batsmen in the world and learn a lot."
Silverwood has no special role models, but rather looks to take the best bits from the best players and adapt them to his game.
"I watch all the great fast bowlers and if I see something I think might work for me I'll try it. I'll take bits from everyone and if it works I'll keep it."
Having achieved his target of playing at least one test, Silverwood has now set his sights on making himself indispensable to the English test side.
"I'll keep working hard, playing hard and make it hard for them not to pick me. I've got to make it difficult for them to leave me out."
England have a home Ashes series against Australia coming up in the middle of the year.
Silverwood would dearly love to be part of that, but prefers not to dwell on it.
"If I get over this hurdle hopefully things like that will take care of themselves.
"What happens here is very important to my international future and I'm concentrating more on what is happening here than what is going to happen in the (English) summer."
England coach David Lloyd has been delighted with Silverwood's progress on tour and predicts a bright future.
"He's strong as an ox, has a massive heart and a never say die' attitude," he said.
"All this nice polite lad stuff, don't worry, he knows what he's up to on the field.
"We're really pleased with him. He's gaining valuable experience and certainly not letting himself down."
